decision: Should WF-106 create a new domain package backend/dsr/page_outreach, or extend an existing one?

state.subject: Trigger outreach on high-intent page visits. A seller's website page view is the trigger. The room owns page-URL targeting rules, a Show-workflow-until frequency mode (Seen / Any interaction happens / Engaged with), a per-session damper, path branching on the buyer's answer, an in-app message, and content_stat receipts.

candidates_examined.page_outreach_new_package: A new backend/dsr/page_outreach package. It owns targeting rules, frequency modes, session damper, branch paths, the in-app message record, and the content_stat receipt record. No existing module reads it.
candidates_examined.extend_visitor_identification: Extend backend/dsr/visitor_identification (WF-031). It already captures page views, URL paths, UTM and referrer, and owns a page-filter grammar in pages.py and paths.py.
candidates_examined.extend_intent_routing: Extend backend/dsr/intent_routing (WF-133). It already evaluates page visits, dwell and repeat thresholds and raises an in-room alert.
candidates_examined.extend_crm_workflows: Extend backend/dsr/crm_workflows (WF-030). It already has a workflow definition object with steps and filter criteria fired off DSR activity.

constraints.package_owns_no_framework: A domain package imports nothing but dsr.store and the standard library.
constraints.no_shared_file_edits: The eleven shared files are protected by a CI guard. backend/dsr/api.py, deps.py, store.py, db/audited.py, seed.py and the frontend shared files cannot be edited.
constraints.tests_must_pass_standalone: The suite runs under pytest-xdist, so each new test file must pass on its own.
constraints.routes_are_discovered: The feature module is mounted by discovery. Its router prefix must be /api/wf-106 and unique.
constraints.parallel_branch_collision_risk: Other agents are merging workflows on the same moving main today. A package two workflows both write to is a merge conflict on files a branch did not name.

state.risk_of_extending: visitor_identification, intent_routing and crm_workflows each belong to a different ticket. A second agent extending the same package on the same day produces a same-file conflict, and the CI guard plus a merged main are the only defences.
state.risk_of_new_package: Duplicated page-path matching and duplicated threshold vocabulary. Both are small, pure and testable, and this project already accepts a small amount of per-workflow vocabulary in exchange for an owned path.

best_approach.instructions: Which candidate best resolves this problem, judged on whether it actually solves it, its risk, and its reversibility?

criteria.page_outreach_new_package: A new backend/dsr/page_outreach package owning targeting rules, frequency modes, the session damper, branch paths and receipts, with no other workflow editing it.
criteria.extend_visitor_identification: Extend backend/dsr/visitor_identification, reusing its capture and page-path grammar.
criteria.extend_intent_routing: Extend backend/dsr/intent_routing, reusing its threshold evaluation and alert record.
criteria.extend_crm_workflows: Extend backend/dsr/crm_workflows, reusing its workflow definition and filter criteria.

decision: WF-106 has two names for one feature module. Which file name should hold the code?

conflict.brief_instruction: TASK.md says these names are exact and must not be shortened, re-slug or renumbered.
conflict.issue_convention: The issue's names are truncated to forty characters, which is this repository's own convention. wf018_read_per_page_dwell_time_and_drop_off_.py and wf020_extract_dsr_viewing_sessions_dwell_tim.py are both forty-character truncations of the same kind of title.

options.what: Delete the forty-character alias. One feature module at the brief's exact name, and the issue's truncated name is absent from the tree.
options.cost: A reader following the GitHub issue to its named file finds nothing at that path.
options.evidence_for: A single module is registered once. The host reports failed_count 0, which several existing test files assert, including backend/tests/test_wf133_http.py.

options.what: Keep both files, the alias re-exporting the brief module's router.
options.cost: Measured, not predicted: the host compares (method, path) across mounted features, finds every one of the eighteen paths already taken, and records the alias as a FAILED feature with a route-collision error. The workflow then appears in both the loaded list and the failed list, and failed_count is 1.
options.evidence_for: Both named paths exist and the alias holds no duplicated code.

options.what: Keep both files, the alias exporting FEATURE and seed but no router, under a second feature id.
options.cost: The registry lists WF-106 twice, so the product shows two nav entries for one workflow and /api/features reports a feature with no prefix and no routes.
options.evidence_for: Both named paths exist and the host raises no collision.

constraints: backend/dsr/api.py cannot be edited, so the host's one-router-per-module rule cannot be changed here.
The host mounts whatever router a feature module exports, so every discovered module must be mountable or harmless.
A duplicate or failed registration of any feature breaks existing tests that assert failed_count == 0, which are other agents' files and must not be edited.

best_approach.instructions: Which option resolves this problem, judged on whether it actually resolves it, its risk, and its reversibility?

criteria.brief_name_only: Delete the alias, ship one module at the brief's exact name, accept that the issue's truncated path is absent.
criteria.alias_reexporting_router: Ship both files with the alias re-exporting the router, accepting that the host records a route collision and failed_count becomes 1.
criteria.alias_without_router: Ship both files with the alias exporting no router under a second feature id, accepting a duplicate registry entry and a second nav entry.

decision: Implementation of WF-106 meets the release bar

state.change_summary: WF-106: browsing-triggered outreach. A new domain package backend/dsr/page_outreach (vocabulary, rules, errors, inferences, engine), a feature module on prefix /api/wf-106 with 18 routes, 292 backend tests in backend/tests/test_wf106.py and test_wf106_http.py, and a frontend feature folder with index.jsx, the page, api.js, primitives.jsx and 63 tests. The researched flow is implemented end to end: a page view is matched against a workflow's targeting rules, the repeat count inside a window is computed, the Show workflow until mode and the researched session damper are applied, a delivery record records what would be shown, and the buyer's answer is recorded as a content_stat receipt. The repeat count, the repeat window and the dwell threshold are this build's derivations; the three frequency modes and the session damper are quoted from the research. Seventeen judgement calls are recorded and served at GET /api/wf-106/inferences, each with the reading taken, what would change it and the risk.

measurements.own_backend_files_result: backend/tests/test_wf106.py and test_wf106_http.py: 292 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, run alone with -n 0 and again together
measurements.whole_backend_suite: 17,604 tests, 14 failures, 2 skipped, 0 errors. All 14 failures are in backend/tests/test_wf056.py, which this branch does not touch. The same 14 fail when tests/test_wf056.py is run on its own with no other file present, so the cause is inside that file and its own subject (WF-056's booking route answering without routeId and with 400 on two writes). The guard reports this branch adds only new files, so a route or response another feature returns cannot have changed.
measurements.coverage_total: 95 percent for dsr over the whole suite, measured with --cov=dsr --cov-report=term:skip-covered. The project gate fails below 90 percent. Four agents were running on eight cores during this measurement, so the number is measured under contention and understates the truth; CI is the authority.
measurements.coverage_this_feature: backend/dsr/page_outreach is 100 percent on all six modules. The feature module is 99 percent; the one uncovered line is the seed's unknown-workflow guard, which a separate test pins unreachable by asserting every demo prospect names a workflow the seed creates.
measurements.routes_called: python tools/verify_all_routes.py --base http://127.0.0.1:8123 called 1,626 routes across 88 features and reported no 5xx and no route that failed to answer. Each of this feature's 18 advertised routes was then called individually and answered with the expected status: 200 for the six reads, 422 for four write routes called empty, 404 for five absent-id reads and one absent-delivery write, 409 on a name taken in that room when driven live.
measurements.live_http_flow: Against uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8123 with the seeded database, the researched chain was driven by hand: workflow created 201, first view recorded and stopped on matched_below_repeat, evaluate reported show without writing, second view showed the block and wrote a delivery, a messenger_opened receipt moved it to hidden_for_session, the same session was then stopped by the damper, a new session showed it again, a path_selected receipt moved it to engaged, and a further view was stopped by the frequency mode. An unpublished interaction kind, a path key nobody declared and a channel with no transport were each refused 422.
measurements.seeder: python backend/seed.py ran this feature's seed and printed: 4 workflows (1 live Engaged with, 1 live Seen, 1 live Any interaction, 1 draft), 13 page views, 4 blocks shown, 3 receipts (1 engaged); prospects: 1 engaged, 1 dismissed, 1 hidden for session, 1 shown and nothing done, 2 not qualified. The string is asserted cp1252-encodable in a test. It is not all successes.

measurements.frontend_build: npm run build: 426 modules transformed, built in 17.16s, no error.

measurements.prettier: npm run format:check: All matched files use Prettier code style. Note that frontend/.prettierignore lists src/features/, so this feature's folder is not among the files Prettier checks; the whole feature set is excluded by design so no branch reformats another's folder.

declared_unverified: No browser verification. The page was rendered under jsdom by vitest, not in a real browser engine, and no screenshot was taken. The build status line 'Verified in localhost browser' stays unticked.
No screen reader was run. Every state pairs its colour with a word and the badge carries an sr-only sentence, but that is a claim from the source, not from an assistive technology.
One browser engine only, and only under jsdom: no Firefox, no WebKit, no narrow viewport.
The seeded demo was inspected through the HTTP surface, not through the page, so the page has not been seen rendering the seeded rows.

state.change_summary: WF-106: browsing-triggered outreach, end to end, and now verified in CI. A new domain package backend/dsr/page_outreach (vocabulary, rules, errors, inferences, engine) holding the pure rules with no framework in it. A feature module on prefix /api/wf-106 with 18 routes. 292 backend tests in backend/tests/test_wf106.py and test_wf106_http.py. A frontend feature folder with index.jsx, the page, api.js, primitives.jsx and 63 tests. The researched chain is implemented: a page view is matched against a workflow's targeting rules, the repeat count inside a window is computed, the researched Show workflow until mode and session damper are applied, a delivery record records what would be shown, and the buyer's answer is recorded as a content_stat receipt. The three frequency modes and the session damper are quoted from the research; the repeat count, the repeat window and the dwell threshold are this build's derivations, labelled sourced False everywhere they are served. Seventeen judgement calls are recorded and served at GET /api/wf-106/inferences, each with the reading taken, what would change it, and the risk. ALL TEN CI CHECKS ON PULL REQUEST 250 PASS, AND THE FIGURES BELOW ARE QUOTED FROM THE CI LOG ITSELF RATHER THAN FROM A LOCAL RUN.
